key_insight: Improvements from LLM-driven evolutionary coding agents often come from retuning, recombining, or simplifying existing strategies and exploiting evaluator specifics rather than primarily inventing wholly new algorithms; the paper presents a taxonomy and empirical analysis to distinguish these mechanisms.
problem_solved: Clarifies what it means when evolutionary coding agents 'improve' — whether gains reflect true algorithmic discovery, parameter/style retuning, recombination of existing code, or evaluator exploitation — so researchers can correctly interpret results and design better evaluation protocols.
method: Run LLM + evolutionary search across benchmark coding/math/algorithm tasks and collect evolved program populations over generations.
Classify evolved outputs into outcome categories (novel algorithmic structure, parameter retuning, recombination, bug‑fix/exploit) via code diffs, behavioral tests, and manual inspection.
Quantify prevalence of each mechanism and validate with ablations and targeted behavioral evaluations to separate genuine innovation from evaluator artifacts.
impact: Helps practitioners interpret progress claims from LLM-driven evolutionary systems, informs design of more robust evaluators and benchmarks, and guides methods that genuinely encourage algorithmic innovation rather than superficial tuning.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of the LLM + evolutionary loop (generate → mutate → evaluate → select) with callouts for where different mechanisms arise
Stacked bar chart showing proportion of evolved solutions by category (novel algorithm / retune / recombination / exploit) across tasks
Before/after code snippets with highlighted diffs to illustrate an example of true structural innovation vs a mere parameter/style change
Scatter plot of population diversity vs best-score improvement over generations, annotated with points labeled by outcome category
paper_title: What Do Evolutionary Coding Agents Evolve?
paper_authors: Nico Pelleriti, Sree Harsha Nelaturu, Zhanke Zhou, Zongze Li, Max Zimmer
